dataset: North Korea (DPRK) tourist access by nationality

entries.basis: DPRK visa policy as reported by operators serving the Russian market (October 2026).

sources.name: Korea Konsult — DPRK tourism status, October 2026
Uri Tours — Air Koryo service update, April 2026

entries.summary: The only nationality currently issued DPRK tourist visas. Russian groups have travelled since February 2024 under limited arrangements, including tours to Pyongyang, the Masikryong ski area and the Wonsan-Kalma resort, booked through Russian operators.

entries.basis: Operator reporting as of October 2026; no DPRK tourist visas issued to Chinese citizens.

sources.name: Korea Konsult — DPRK tourism status, October 2026
Yonhap News Agency — China–DPRK passenger trains resume, March 2026

entries.summary: Chinese tourists cannot currently enter the DPRK as tourists, even though Beijing–Pyongyang passenger trains resumed in March 2026 and Air China flights resumed the same month. Those services carry officials, DPRK nationals and business-visa holders, not tour groups.

entries.basis: US Department of State, Public Notice 13073 (Federal Register, 20 July 2026); US travel advisory Level 4: Do Not Travel.

sources.name: US Department of State — Public Notice 13073, Federal Register
Koryo Tours — Can US citizens travel to North Korea?

entries.summary: US passports are invalid for travel to, in, or through North Korea unless specially validated by the State Department. The restriction, in force since 1 September 2017, was extended to 31 August 2027. Special validation is granted only in very limited national-interest categories (journalism, Red Cross missions, compelling humanitarian cases) — never for tourism. The DPRK also bars US dual nationals regardless of the passport used.

entries.basis: DPRK admission practice as reported by specialist operators.

sources.name: Korea Konsult — DPRK tourism status, October 2026

entries.summary: South Korean nationals are not admitted to the DPRK as tourists. Dual nationals holding South Korean citizenship are excluded even when travelling on another passport, including during the February 2025 Rason window and marathon delegations.

entries.basis: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Malaysia — official travel ban statement, 28 September 2017.

sources.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Malaysia — travel ban statement
Nikkei Asia — Malaysia imposes travel ban for North Korea, 2017

entries.summary: Malaysia's government has banned all Malaysian citizens from travelling to North Korea since 28 September 2017, until further notice. The two countries have had no diplomatic relations since 2021.

entries.basis: DPRK visa suspension (operator reporting); UK FCDO travel advice.

sources.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — North Korea travel advice

entries.summary: British passport holders face no UK legal ban, but the DPRK is not issuing tourist visas to them. The UK Foreign Office advises against all but essential travel to North Korea. British travellers joined the February–March 2025 Rason tours before access was suspended again.

sources.name: Korea JoongAng Daily — Rason tours suspended, March 2025
Korea Konsult — DPRK tourism status, October 2026

entries.summary: EU citizens face no EU-wide legal ban, but the DPRK is not issuing tourist visas to them. EU nationals took part in the February 2025 Rason tours and the April 2025 Pyongyang Marathon delegation; both channels are closed again.

entries.basis: DPRK admission practice for the 2025–2026 limited windows (operator reporting).

sources.name: Uri Tours — Is North Korea open for tourism? FAQ, 2026

entries.summary: Japanese nationals were excluded even from the limited openings offered to other foreigners: they were not admitted during the February 2025 Rason window and were excluded from the planned 2026 Pyongyang Marathon. No tourist visas are being issued.

sources.name: Korea Konsult — DPRK tourism status, October 2026

entries.summary: No tourist visas are being issued to any nationality other than Russia. Australians, Canadians and others visited during the February 2025 Rason window and the April 2025 marathon delegation; both closed within weeks. Specialist operators are taking waitlist registrations only.

method: Every status is checked against at least two independent sources — or, where the fact is the text of a rule itself, the one primary official source that states it — preferring official government notices and specialist tour operators. See https://northkoreahub.com/about/method/

status_key.banned: Travel is prohibited, either by the traveller's own government or by the DPRK.
status_key.open: Tourist visas are being issued and tours are running.
status_key.restricted: Tourism is possible only in a limited form (e.g. approved group tours via specific operators).
status_key.suspended: Tourism is not currently possible, but there is no home-country legal ban; the block is on the DPRK side.
